site_ui.lead: Follow practitioners as they trace living relatives through family trees, newspapers, and vital records, test competing identities, and document the kinship behind inheritance searches.
site_ui.summary: All 12 chapters synthesize 192 verbatim YouTube practitioner testimonies with timestamped inline attribution. Practitioners describe relationship checks, missing-beneficiary searches, research documentation, fee arrangements, and cases where newly discovered wills or closer relatives changed the outcome.

flow: Run preliminary research to assess the fit with your skills; check available funds and other claimants before extending fieldwork.
Start with known relationships, existing sources, family photographs, and inherited papers; search locality-specific catalogs, newspapers, and vital records.
Build sourced parent-child links and follow whole families, including siblings and unmarried relatives; read multiple obituary versions for additional leads.
Distinguish same-named households and biological, foster, step, and half relationships; use PBI’s two-source relationship check and second-reviewer approach.

Investigate wills and possible closer relatives before treating a wider family as entitled; pursue contact through existing numbers, relatives, and field visits, and verify suspicious letters independently.
Record sources, negative findings, unresolved relationships, and contact efforts; use reusable report and citation templates to prepare documented findings.
